vuln_id: ARVO arvo:8241 / OpenSSL session-ticket stale-session use-after-free

classification.classification_note: A raw `session_ticket` extension can be materialized into `pre_proc_exts`, decrypted into `sess`, freed on the trailing-bytes path without being nulled, and later dereferenced through `ret->ssl_version` in `ssl_get_prev_session()`.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists where the variable sess is not set to NULL after being freed, which can lead to use-after-free issues.
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is a 369-byte harness input file, but `fuzz/server.c` strips the final byte `0x20` into `opt` and writes only the first 368 bytes into the input BIO. That 368-byte prefix is a TLS ClientHello whose extension block contains `00 23 00 a0` at offset `0xa0`, so `tls_collect_extensions()` stores a 160-byte `session_ticket` body in `clienthello->pre_proc_exts[TLSEXT_IDX_session_ticket]`. During resumption processing `ssl_get_prev_session()` calls `tls_get_ticket_from_client()`, which forwards those raw ticket bytes into `tls_decrypt_ticket()`. The decryptor parses the ticket with `d2i_SSL_SESSION()` to materialize a heap `SSL_SESSION`, then subtracts the consumed prefix from `slen`. On the crashing witness `sess` is non-NULL but `slen != 0`, so the decrypted ticket contains trailing bytes beyond the serialized session. Vulnerable `tls_decrypt_ticket()` frees `sess`, sets `ret = SSL_TICKET_NO_DECRYPT`, skips the optional `decrypt_ticket_cb` block because no callback is installed in this staged harness, and then publishes the stale pointer through `*psess = sess;`. `ssl_get_prev_session()` receives nonfatal status `SSL_TICKET_NO_DECRYPT` together with the dangling `ret`, breaks out of its switch without clearing `ret`, bypasses the `ret == NULL` guard, and reads `ret->ssl_version`, producing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free READ. The staged patch fixes the lifetime bug by inserting `sess = NULL` immediately after `SSL_SESSION_free(sess);`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the vulnerability-relevant input. The built-in extension table entry at `extensions.c:203-208` is `TLSEXT_TYPE_session_ticket`, and `tls_collect_extensions()` stores that raw extension body into the matching `RAW_EXTENSION` slot later reached as `hello->pre_proc_exts[TLSEXT_IDX_session_ticket]`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` file is 369 bytes with SHA-256 `3ed2e6a6c7c38ae868e4a6aafc6246cfe0e9bd7574e0545da6146e1aec83f464`. `fuzz/server.c` strips the final byte `0x20` into `opt` and writes only the first 368 bytes into the input BIO; that consumed prefix has SHA-256 `701473a23d5cd518f57e95142075085e93e6843adcf26dc2b3a7bd13adb74506`. Within that 368-byte prefix, offset `0xa0` contains `00 23 00 a0`, so `tls_collect_extensions()` sees extension type `0x0023` (`session_ticket`) with a 160-byte body and stores that body here.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.code:
sess = d2i_SSL_SESSION(NULL, &p, slen);
slen -= p - sdec;
tainted_value_origin.description: The decrypted ticket plaintext is materialized here as a heap `SSL_SESSION *`, and the parser cursor subtraction computes how many attacker-derived bytes remain unconsumed. The saved crash requires both witnessed facts: `sess` is non-NULL and the remainder `slen` stays nonzero.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `ssl_get_prev_session()` treats the dangling `ret` returned from `tls_get_ticket_from_client()` as a live resumed session and reads `ret->ssl_version` from freed `SSL_SESSION` storage.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer report is `heap-use-after-free READ of size 4` at `ssl/ssl_sess.c:593:14` in `ssl_get_prev_session`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. On the trailing-bytes consistency-failure path, `tls_decrypt_ticket()` frees `sess` but does not clear the local pointer before the shared epilogue publishes it through `*psess`, so the caller receives a dangling non-NULL `SSL_SESSION *`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `sess = NULL;` immediately after this free. That makes the later `*psess = sess;` publish `NULL` instead of a freed pointer, so `ssl_get_prev_session()` takes its `ret == NULL` path instead of dereferencing stale memory.

bio_write_prefix_only.description: The harness consumes the staged 369-byte file by splitting off the last byte into `opt` and writing only the first 368 bytes into OpenSSL's input BIO.

parser_admitted.description: The ClientHello parser accepts the raw extensions block and materializes `clienthello->pre_proc_exts`, so later resumption logic can index `TLSEXT_IDX_session_ticket` instead of rejecting the handshake earlier.

callback_unset.description: The staged harness creates a fresh `SSL_CTX` and never calls `SSL_CTX_set_session_ticket_cb()`. Because `SSL_CTX_new()` zero-initializes the context via `OPENSSL_zalloc()` in `ssl/ssl_lib.c:2890`, `ctx->decrypt_ticket_cb` remains NULL and the callback block in `tls_decrypt_ticket()` cannot clear `sess` before publication.

evidence_limitations: The staged artifacts prove only the observed predicate `slen != 0` after `d2i_SSL_SESSION()` and do not expose the decrypted ticket plaintext or exact leftover-byte count.

fine_trace.note: Source. For the consumed 368-byte ClientHello prefix, the extension header at offset `0xa0` is `00 23 00 a0`, so when the collector reaches type `TLSEXT_TYPE_session_ticket` it stores the 160-byte body into the `RAW_EXTENSION` entry later indexed as `TLSEXT_IDX_session_ticket`.

`tls_get_ticket_from_client()` retrieves that stored `session_ticket` entry from `hello->pre_proc_exts`, confirms it is present for the staged witness, computes `size == 160`, and forwards its raw bytes into `tls_decrypt_ticket()`.

`d2i_SSL_SESSION()` parses the decrypted ticket plaintext into a new heap `SSL_SESSION *`. AddressSanitizer's allocation stack for the later-freed 520-byte region goes through this call into `SSL_SESSION_new()`.

After `d2i_SSL_SESSION()` advances parse cursor `p`, the code subtracts the consumed prefix from `slen`. On the crashing witness this remainder stays nonzero, showing the decrypted ticket contains trailing bytes after the serialized session; the staged artifacts do not expose the exact leftover count.
The trailing-bytes consistency check is taken for the staged witness. Because not all decrypted bytes were consumed, the ticket is rejected instead of being accepted as a resumed session.
Root-cause step. The trailing-bytes branch frees the heap `SSL_SESSION`, but vulnerable code leaves local `sess` pointing at the freed allocation.
The same branch records the outcome as `SSL_TICKET_NO_DECRYPT` and jumps to the shared epilogue, so the caller will later treat this path as a nonfatal ticket miss rather than a fatal error.

fine_trace.code:
if (s->session_ctx->decrypt_ticket_cb != NULL
        && (ret == SSL_TICKET_EMPTY
            || ret == SSL_TICKET_NO_DECRYPT
            || ret == SSL_TICKET_SUCCESS
            || ret == SSL_TICKET_SUCCESS_RENEW)) {
fine_trace.note: The optional callback cleanup block is skipped in the staged setup. `ret` now qualifies, but `s->session_ctx->decrypt_ticket_cb` is still NULL because the harness only creates `ctx = SSL_CTX_new(SSLv23_method())` and never calls `SSL_CTX_set_session_ticket_cb()`, whose setter would populate this field.

With no `decrypt_ticket_cb` to clear or replace `sess`, the shared epilogue stores the freed pointer through `*psess`. This publishes a dangling non-NULL session pointer alongside the previously selected `SSL_TICKET_NO_DECRYPT` status.
The caller materializes both outputs from `tls_get_ticket_from_client()`: `ret` receives the freed `SSL_SESSION *`, and `r` receives the nonfatal status returned from step 7.

fine_trace.code:
case SSL_TICKET_NO_DECRYPT:
case SSL_TICKET_SUCCESS:
case SSL_TICKET_SUCCESS_RENEW:

fine_trace.note: The `switch (r)` explicitly treats `SSL_TICKET_NO_DECRYPT` as a nonfatal case and just `break`s. This preserves the dangling `ret` instead of sending execution to the fatal `err` path.
The only direct pointer sanity check is `ret == NULL`. It is bypassed because the stale pointer is non-NULL, so execution falls through to field validation.
ASan sink. The first field read from the supposed resumed session dereferences freed `SSL_SESSION` storage. The saved report is `READ of size 4` at this line.

format.name: OpenSSL server harness input with a 368-byte ClientHello prefix and 1-byte option suffix
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged 369-byte file whose final byte `0x20` is consumed by the harness as `opt`, while only the first 368 bytes are written into OpenSSL as the TLS record stream. That 368-byte prefix contains a `session_ticket` extension header `00 23 00 a0` at offset `0xa0`, and the saved Stage 01 crash proves this exact witness drives `d2i_SSL_SESSION()` to return non-NULL while leaving at least one unconsumed decrypted byte (`slen != 0`). Those witnessed states make `tls_decrypt_ticket()` free `sess`, leave it non-NULL, return `SSL_TICKET_NO_DECRYPT`, and later let `ssl_get_prev_session()` read `ret->ssl_version` from freed storage. This contract is limited to this exact witness and inputs that preserve the same non-NULL-session plus trailing-bytes state.
